overview.title: 📖 Overview: Hillel's Patience, Shammai's Impatience, and Fear of Heaven
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 31a–31b
overview.hebrewSource: עַל שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת בִּשְׁעַת לֵידָתָן: עַל שֶׁאֵינָן זְהִירוֹת בַּנִּדָּה, בַּחַלָּה, וּבְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Continuing from the previous daf's teaching to be patient like Hillel and not impatient like Shammai, the Gemara tells four vivid stories: a man who bets 400 zuz that he can anger Hillel with mocking ethnic questions, and three gentiles who come to convert on outrageous conditions — accepting only the Written Torah, learning the whole Torah 'on one foot,' and becoming High Priest. Shammai rebuffs each; Hillel converts all three and teaches them Torah's substance through patience. The Gemara then explores fear of Heaven as the foundation beneath Torah study, with Reish Lakish mapping the six orders of Mishna onto a verse in Isaiah, and Rava describing the questions a soul faces after death. The daf's aggadic run on lighting the Shabbat lamp then closes with a new mishna: women die in childbirth for negligence in three mitzvot — niddah, separating ḥalla, and kindling the Shabbat lamp — and the Gemara explains why negligence in each corresponds to danger specifically in childbirth.

slides.title: 😤 The Wager to Anger Hillel
slides.subtitle: Three mocking questions, three patient answers

steps.content: 1️⃣ Two men bet 400 zuz that one can provoke Hillel to anger; he interrupts Hillel's Shabbat-eve hair-washing three times with mocking ethnic questions
2️⃣ 'Why are Babylonians' heads oval?' Hillel: 'A significant question — their midwives lack skill'
3️⃣ 'Why are Tadmoreans' eyes bleary?' Hillel: 'They live among the sands'
4️⃣ 'Why are Africans' feet wide?' Hillel: 'They live in marshlands'
5️⃣ The man reveals he lost 400 zuz because of Hillel's calm; Hillel replies: better to lose 400 zuz twice over than for Hillel to lose his patience

slides.title: 🕎 Three Would-Be Converts: Shammai vs. Hillel
slides.subtitle: Each demanded something impossible; each was handled differently
rows: Convert me, teaching only the Written Torah
Converted him; on day two reversed the alphabet, proving reliance on oral transmission is unavoidable
Teach me the whole Torah while I stand on one foot
Pushed him away with his builder's cubit
'What is hateful to you, do not do to another — that is the whole Torah; the rest is commentary. Go study.'
Convert me so I can become High Priest
Pushed him away with his builder's cubit
Converted him and taught him Torah, including 'the stranger who draws near shall be put to death' — even King David

callout.label: The converts' verdict:
callout.text: All three later met and agreed: 'Shammai's impatience sought to drive us from the world; Hillel's patience brought us under the wings of the Divine Presence.'

slides.title: 👑 Learning Royal Protocol From the Torah
slides.subtitle: The convert reasons an a fortiori from David himself
slides.label: The teaching:
slides.text: Hillel told the would-be High Priest that one must first learn 'the protocols of royalty' — meaning, study Torah. When the convert reached 'the stranger who draws near shall be put to death' (Numbers 1:51) and asked about whom it spoke, Hillel answered: 'Even King David.' The convert reasoned: if this restriction applies even to Israel, God's beloved children, all the more so to a convert who arrived with nothing but his staff and bag. He returned to Hillel and thanked him for bringing him under the wings of the Divine Presence, retracting his demand to be made High Priest.

slides.title: 📚 Fear of Heaven: The Foundation Beneath Torah
slides.subtitle: Two teachings on why fear of Heaven must come first

boxes.title: Reish Lakish — Isaiah 33:6
items: Maps six words of the verse to the Six Orders of Mishna (Zeraim, Moed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, Teharot)
Concludes: even after mastering all six, 'the fear of the Lord is his treasure' — the true prize

boxes.title: Rabba bar Rav Huna — the Treasurer
items: One who has Torah but not fear of Heaven is like a treasurer given the inner keys but not the outer
He cannot even enter to use what he holds
Rabbi Yannai: 'Woe to one who builds a gate but has no courtyard'

callout.label: Rava's postmortem questions:
callout.text: Did you deal faithfully in business? Did you fix times for Torah? Did you engage in procreation? Did you hope for salvation? Did you debate wisely? — yet all depend on whether fear of the Lord was one's treasure.

slides.title: 🕯️ New Mishna: Three Sins, Danger in Childbirth
slides.subtitle: Why negligence in each mitzva corresponds to this specific risk

nodes.content: 📜 Mishna: women die in childbirth for negligence in three mitzvot — niddah, ḥalla, and lighting the Shabbat lamp
🩸 Niddah (Rabbi Yitzḥak): 'She sinned in the chambers of her womb; therefore she is punished in the chambers of her womb' — measure for measure
❓ But why do ḥalla and lighting the lamp also correspond to this danger?
✅ The Galilean's teaching before Rav Ḥisda: 'I placed a quarter-log of blood in you [at creation] — about matters of blood I warned you,' linking all three to the peril of blood in childbirth

summary.principle: Hillel's patience — with a provocateur and with three outrageous converts — models the fear of Heaven that the Gemara insists must underlie all Torah study, and the daf's aggadic sequence on the Shabbat lamp closes with the mishna on why women's negligence in niddah, ḥalla, and lighting endangers them specifically in childbirth.

quiz.q: How did Hillel respond when a man tried to provoke him with three mocking questions about different peoples, hoping to win a bet?
o: He grew angry and threw the man out
He answered each question calmly and respectfully, without losing his temper
He refused to answer any of the questions
He reported the man to the court
quiz.e: Hillel patiently and respectfully answered each mocking question, refusing to become angry even after the man revealed he had wagered 400 zuz on provoking him.

quiz.q: What did Hillel tell the gentile who asked to be converted and taught the entire Torah while standing on one foot?
o: That such a request was impossible and pushed him away
'That which is hateful to you, do not do to another — that is the whole Torah; the rest is commentary. Go study.'
That he must first become a priest
That the Torah cannot be summarized at all
quiz.e: Unlike Shammai, who pushed the man away with a builder's cubit, Hillel converted him and offered this concise formulation of the Torah's essence.

quiz.q: How did the would-be High Priest convert come to retract his demand, according to the Gemara?
o: Hillel refused to convert him

By studying Torah with Hillel, he reasoned an a fortiori from the verse 'the stranger who draws near shall be put to death,' realizing that if this restriction applies even to King David, it certainly applies to him
He was told converts cannot serve in the Temple at all
Shammai eventually convinced him
quiz.e: Hillel taught him that learning 'royal protocol' meant studying Torah; reaching Numbers 1:51, the convert reasoned that if even David was bound by this restriction, he certainly was too, and he abandoned his demand.

quiz.q: According to Rabba bar Rav Huna's parable, what is a person with Torah knowledge but no fear of Heaven comparable to?
o: A king without a crown
A treasurer who was given the keys to the inner chambers but not the outer door, so he cannot even enter
A farmer without seeds
A judge without a court
quiz.e: Rabba bar Rav Huna compares such a person to a treasurer with only inner keys — the Torah (inner treasure) is inaccessible without fear of Heaven (the outer key).

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, for negligence in which three mitzvot are women punished specifically during childbirth?
o: Prayer, charity, and Torah study
Niddah, separating ḥalla, and lighting the Shabbat lamp
Fasting, tzedakah, and tefillin
Kashrut, Shabbat, and honoring parents
quiz.e: The mishna states that women die in childbirth for negligence in three mitzvot: the laws of menstrual purity (niddah), separating ḥalla from dough, and kindling the Shabbat lamp.
